transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi... yeah, thanks. Um, so I guess the main thing, the thing that really made me finally ask for help—because, you know, I've been putting it off for a bit, just thinking it was a phase or whatever—is that I just... I barely want to eat anymore. At all. It's getting ridiculous, honestly. 

Like, I work retail, so I'm on my feet all day at the store, dealing with customers, running back and forth to the stockroom, and usually by midday I'd be absolutely starving. But lately, I'll go on my lunch break, and I'll get something I usually love, and I just sit there. I'll be in the break room in the back just staring at this food that I used to really like. I'll unwrap it, look at it, and my stomach just... it has zero interest. I'll sit there for my whole thirty-minute break just staring at a sandwich or whatever, maybe I'll take one bite and just chew it forever, and then I end up just throwing most of it away in the trash can by the lockers before I clock back in. It's every single day now. I'm wasting so much money buying food I just chuck in the garbage, but I just have absolutely no desire to actually eat any of it.
Have you lost any weight recently?

Yeah, I mean, I definitely must have, because like I was just saying, I'm practically living on nothing right now since I just keep throwing my lunches in the trash. I don't actually own a scale at my apartment, so I couldn't tell you an exact number of pounds or anything like that, but I can definitely feel it in my clothes. 

Like, we have this strict dress code at the store, right? We have to wear these specific khaki pants, and I used to just throw them on and they fit perfectly fine. But the last couple of weeks, I've had to start wearing this old belt pulled really tight, otherwise they literally start sliding down my waist when I'm bending over to pick up boxes or moving pallets in the stockroom. My manager even made a comment the other day about my uniform looking baggy and asked if I needed to order a new size. 

So yeah, I've definitely lost weight, but it's all just because of what I was telling you—I just barely want to eat anymore. It's exactly why I finally made this appointment, because you can't just stare at food you used to like, throw most of it away every single day, and expect your body not to shrink, you know? It's just... I'm shrinking out of my clothes and I still can't force myself to take a bite.
Do you think there's anything on your mind or any feelings that might be contributing to your lack of interest in food?

I mean... I really don't know. I've actually spent a lot of time trying to figure that out myself, to be honest. Because it doesn't make any sense, right? Like, I'll be standing there at the front register, ringing people up for hours, just scanning barcodes and bagging stuff, and I'll try to think to myself, "Am I stressed about something? Is there something specific bothering me?" But honestly, I can't really point to one single thing. 

It's not like I'm sitting in the break room dwelling on some huge problem or stressing over a fight with somebody. I mean, sure, money is always tight when you're working retail, and paying bills is always kind of a headache, but that's just normal life stuff, you know? It's nothing new that would suddenly make me stop wanting my lunch. I've spent whole shifts just breaking down cardboard boxes in the back alley, trying to rack my brain to see if I'm subconsciously worried about something, but I just come up with nothing. 

There's no big thought or feeling blocking me from eating. I'll look at a sandwich and my brain is just... blank. It's really frustrating, because if I knew what was on my mind causing it, maybe I could just deal with it and finally eat a normal meal again, but right now... yeah, I just don't have a reason for it. I just don't know.
Do you think you are underweight or at a normal weight right now?

I mean, I don't really know if I'd say I'm officially underweight or anything like that. Like I said, I don't have a scale, so I can't give you a number to prove it one way or the other. I just know I'm definitely smaller than I was, you know, a month or two ago. 

But as for being underweight... I mean, I'm not, like, skin and bones or anything. I don't look in the mirror and think I look sick or starving, even though I'm barely eating. I just look... I don't know, a little deflated? Like I mentioned with the uniform pants, they're definitely looser, and I have to pull my belt tighter, but it's not like I'm swimming in them to the point where they're falling off my hips completely. It's just enough to be annoying when I'm trying to work. 

I guess if you looked at a chart or something, maybe I'd still be considered a normal weight for my height? I'm pretty average height, so I feel like I'd have to lose a lot more before someone would look at me on the street and think, "Wow, that guy needs to eat a burger." It's just... I know my own body, and I know I'm smaller than my normal, but I couldn't tell you if that means I've crossed some line into being officially underweight. I just know I'm shrinking because of the whole food thing, and that's what's freaking me out more than the actual size I am right now.
Are you afraid of gaining weight?

No, no, definitely not. It's not like that at all. I mean, honestly, if anything, I'd really prefer it if things just went back to normal and I could put the weight back on. Because like I was saying, dealing with these uniform pants is just a huge hassle right now. You know, when you're working an eight-hour shift on your feet, running back and forth from the register to the stockroom, the last thing you want to be thinking about is whether your pants are going to slide down while you're carrying a heavy box of inventory. 

And it's just... it's exhausting, really. I don't want to be shrinking. I don't look at myself and think, "Oh good, I'm losing weight." It's actually the opposite. I'm looking at my clothes not fitting right and thinking, "Man, I really wish I could just sit down and eat a normal lunch like I used to." Like, I used to love going on my break and getting a decent meal, and now it's just this whole ordeal where I'm throwing it away. 

So, no, I'm not afraid of gaining weight. If I could just wake up tomorrow and have my appetite back, and eat enough to fill my clothes out properly again so my manager stops looking at me funny, I would do it in a heartbeat. It's just that my brain or my stomach or whatever just won't let me do it right now. But the idea of gaining the weight back? No, that doesn't scare me at all. I'd actually welcome it, to be honest.
Do you think you look too fat or too thin when you look in the mirror?

I mean, when I look in the mirror... like, say I'm getting ready for my shift, right? I usually drag myself into the bathroom, and the lighting in my apartment is really harsh, just those cheap, bright overhead bulbs my landlord put in. And I'll just stand there while I'm brushing my teeth or whatever, just kind of looking at myself in the glass. And honestly... no, I don't think I look too fat, and I don't look at myself and think I'm way too thin, either. 

It's not like I'm seeing a skeleton staring back at me or anything dramatic like that. Like I was saying earlier about the uniform, I know I've lost some weight because of how my pants are fitting around the waist, but my actual reflection? It mostly just looks like regular me. Just... I don't know, maybe a little tired, maybe a little less filled out in the face, but definitely not "too thin." 

It's weird because you'd think if your belt needs tightening, you'd look in the mirror and see this shocking difference, but I really just see the same guy. Maybe a little washed out from the fluorescent lights, but that's about it. So, yeah, I don't look in the mirror and obsess over being too big or too small. I just see myself. It's just frustrating to look at yourself and know something is off with your appetite, but your reflection doesn't even really show it that much, you know? I just look pretty much average.
Are you worried about eating because of something it might do to you besides making you gain weight?

Well, I mean... no, I'm not worried about gaining weight, like I said. And it's not like I think the food is poisoned or contaminated or anything crazy like that, if that's what you mean. It's just... I don't know, it's hard to explain without sounding weird, but it's just this overwhelming feeling of dread when I even think about eating. 

Like yesterday, for example, I was in the breakroom at work. I had this sandwich I made—just turkey and cheese, nothing special, the same thing I've made a hundred times. And I was sitting there, looking at it, and my stomach was completely in knots. Not because I thought it was going to make me sick or anything, but just... the whole act of eating it just felt impossible. It felt like if I took a bite, everything would just go wrong. Not physically wrong, just... wrong. 

And my coworker, Dave, he was sitting across from me eating this huge slice of pizza, and he kept looking at me like I was crazy because I was just staring at my sandwich for like ten minutes straight. I wanted to eat it, I really did, because my stomach was actually rumbling and I was feeling a little lightheaded from standing at the register all morning, but I just couldn't bring myself to do it. It's like my brain puts up this massive brick wall between me and the food, and I can't climb over it, no matter how hungry I am or how much my pants are falling down. 

So, no, I don't think the food is going to do something bad to me, like make me sick or hurt me. It's just this intense, paralyzing feeling that I shouldn't eat it. And it's so frustrating because I know it doesn't make any logical sense. I know it's just a turkey sandwich. But in that moment, sitting in the breakroom with the humming of the vending machine and Dave chewing his pizza, it felt like the hardest thing in the world to just take a bite. So I ended up just throwing it in the trash again and going back to the floor with an empty stomach. It's just exhausting, honestly.
Do you feel anxious when you think about the act of eating?

Yeah, I guess anxious is a good word for it. Or just... overwhelmed, maybe? It's just... honestly, this whole food thing, it's actually what made me finally ask for help in the first place. Because I just barely want to eat anymore. Like, at all. 

Like I was telling you about that turkey sandwich yesterday... it's not just a one-time thing, it's happening pretty much every day now. I'll be on my lunch break at the store, just sitting there at that wobbly table in the breakroom, and I'll be staring at food that I used to really like. Like, stuff I used to genuinely look forward to halfway through a long shift, you know? Maybe a sub from the place next door, or even just my favorite chips from the vending machine. And I just sit there staring at it. My brain just completely locks up, and the idea of chewing and swallowing feels like this massive, impossible chore. 

So I just end up throwing most of it away. And that's... that's when I realized I needed to come see somebody. Because you can't just survive on nothing while you're unloading heavy pallets in the stockroom and dealing with customers all day, right? You just can't. I used to be the guy who could crush a whole pizza by myself after a closing shift, no problem. And now I'm the guy tossing perfectly good, expensive food into the breakroom trash can while my coworkers stare at me. It's just a waste of money, it's a waste of food, and it makes me feel crazy. So yeah, I guess thinking about trying to force it down does make me anxious, because I know how it's going to end up—with me just staring at it until my break is over and tossing it out.
Is there something specific about the act of eating itself that scares you or makes you anxious?

Well, no... not exactly. I mean, it's not like the chewing or the swallowing itself is scary. It's not like I'm afraid I'm going to choke on it or that my throat is going to close up or anything physical like that. I know some people have that, where they get really freaked out about swallowing pills or food, but it's not that for me. 

It's more just... I don't know, it's like the whole process just feels completely wrong. Like I said before with the sandwich, it's just this heavy, awful feeling that washes over me. Like I'm doing something I really shouldn't be doing. And then I start overthinking it. I'll be sitting there, holding this piece of bread, and suddenly I'm just hyper-aware of everything. The texture of it, the smell, the way my jaw is supposed to move... and it all just feels so pointless and exhausting. 

Like yesterday, after I threw the sandwich away, I went back out to the floor and I was trying to stock the shelves in the cereal aisle. And I was just looking at all these boxes of cereal, all these bright colors and cartoon characters, and thinking about how weird it is that we all just shove this stuff into our faces every day. It just felt so absurd. So, it's not the act of eating that scares me, like in a phobia kind of way. It's just that my brain refuses to cooperate with the idea of it. It just shuts down completely, and the anxiety comes from knowing that I'm supposed to be doing this normal, everyday thing, and I just... can't. And then I have to go back to work and pretend everything is fine while my stomach is completely empty.
Is there something specific that you're afraid might happen if you eat?

No, no, it's not like that. I'm not afraid that, like, my stomach is going to explode or that the food is going to turn into poison in my body or anything crazy like that. I'm not scared of the food itself, and I'm not scared of what it's going to do to me. I know it's just food. I know it's supposed to give me energy. It's just... I just don't want it. At all. 

I know I keep talking about this, but it's really the main thing that made me finally call and ask for an appointment. Because I just barely want to eat anymore. Like, ever. And it's not a fear thing, it's a... a complete lack of desire thing. I'll be sitting there on my lunch break at the store—usually in that one chair by the window that squeaks every time you move—and I'll have this food in front of me. Food that I actually used to really like. Like, I used to go out of my way to get this specific spicy chicken sandwich from the deli down the street, right? I'd look forward to it all morning while I was ringing up customers. And now, I can go get that exact same sandwich, sit down, unwrap it, smell it... and nothing. There's just zero drive to eat it. 

I'll just sit there staring at it, picking at the wrapper, maybe taking a tiny bite of the crust just to see if I can force it, and it just feels like chewing cardboard. So I just end up throwing most of it away. And I hate doing it, because it's a waste of money, and my manager, Sarah, she's always making comments about how I'm wasting good food, but I just can't bring myself to finish it. It's not fear. It's just... I don't want it. My appetite is just completely gone, and that's what's so weird to me, because I used to be such a big eater.
Do you feel sad or depressed when you think about eating?

Sad? Um... no, I wouldn't say sad. Or depressed, really. Not about the food itself, anyway. It's not like I look at a piece of pizza or a sandwich and start crying or feeling really down or anything like that. It's more just... blank, I guess? Like I was saying before about being in the breakroom, sitting in that squeaky chair by the window. When I unwrap the food, I don't feel this big wave of sadness. I don't really feel much of anything, honestly, except maybe just tired. It's just this heavy, dull feeling of knowing I'm supposed to do this thing, but I just have absolutely zero drive to actually do it. 

I mean, I guess if I feel sad at all, it's just about the whole situation in general, you know? Like, it definitely bums me out that I'm wasting so much money, especially on an hourly retail wage, and that my manager Sarah keeps getting on my case or making those little comments about me throwing away perfectly good food. That part sucks. But the actual thought of eating? No, that doesn't make me depressed. It's just... it's just a chore. A really exhausting chore that I don't want to do. 

Like yesterday when I was stocking those cereal boxes... I wasn't sad looking at them. Just kind of disconnected from the whole idea of it. So yeah, no, thinking about eating doesn't make me sad. It just makes me feel exhausted because I know exactly how the whole routine is going to play out, with me just staring at it, picking at the crust, and then tossing it in the trash while my coworkers are enjoying their lunch. But it's not a sad feeling, if that makes sense.
Is there something specific that happens when you try to eat that makes you stop?

Well, it's like I was saying before, it's just this complete... wall that I hit. It's not that I start choking or anything physically stops me. It's just that I barely want to eat anymore, which, honestly, is the whole reason I finally picked up the phone and asked for help. I just couldn't ignore it anymore. 

I'll be sitting there in the breakroom on my lunch break at the store, right? And I'll have this food in front of me, food that I used to really like, like that spicy chicken sandwich I told you about, or even just a slice of pizza from the place next door. I used to devour that stuff. But now, I just sit there staring at it. I unwrap it, I look at it, I might even bring it up to my mouth, and then... nothing. I just stop. My brain just says, "Nope, we're not doing this." 

I'll pick at it, maybe tear off a little piece of the bread, but the actual act of chewing and swallowing just feels like climbing a mountain. So I just end up throwing most of it away. I'll wrap it back up, trying to be subtle about it so Sarah doesn't see and make another comment, and I just toss it in the garbage. And it's every single day now. I just stare at it, realize I have absolutely zero desire to put it in my body, and throw it out. That's what happens. It's just a total lack of wanting it, and it's what made me realize I really needed to come talk to someone, because it's just not normal for me to throw away perfectly good food like that.
Is there a particular taste or smell of food that you find especially unappealing?

No, it's not a specific taste or smell, or like, certain types of food turning me off. It's really just everything. Like I was saying, I can have that spicy chicken sandwich right under my nose, and the smell of it used to make my mouth water, you know? I used to love the way the bread smelled toasted, and the spices on the chicken... but now, it just doesn't register as something I want. It's not that it smells bad or tastes gross, it's just... I don't care about it. 

Honestly, I feel like a broken record, but this whole thing, this complete lack of appetite, is really what pushed me to finally call and ask for help. Because it's just so strange for me. Like, I'll be sitting there on my lunch break at the store—in that squeaky chair, looking out the window at the parking lot—just staring at this food. Food that I used to really like, food that I spent my hard-earned money on, and I just... I can't do it. I just end up throwing most of it away. 

And it doesn't matter if it's the chicken sandwich, or pizza, or a salad, or even just a bag of chips from the vending machine near the manager's office. It all just seems pointless to eat. The smell doesn't bother me, the taste doesn't bother me... it's just that the whole idea of eating anything at all is just totally gone. I just stare at it, pick at it a little, and then toss it in the trash. And I know Sarah is probably judging me every time she hears the trash can lid shut, but I just can't bring myself to care about the food anymore. That's what's so weird, and that's why I'm here, because I just barely want to eat anymore, no matter what it is.
Do you find that you have no appetite at certain times of the day, or is it the same all day long?

It's pretty much the same all day long, honestly. It doesn't really matter if it's breakfast time before my shift, or dinner time when I get home to my apartment, or... or like I keep saying, right in the middle of the day during my lunch break. It's just a constant thing now. I wake up, and there's just no hunger there. I'll think, 'Okay, I should probably make some toast or pour a bowl of cereal,' but the thought just kind of sits there in my head and goes nowhere. 

And then I go to work, and I'm on my feet for hours, dealing with customers, stocking shelves, moving boxes around in the back room—stuff that used to make me starving by the time noon rolled around. But now, when my break finally hits and I go sit in the breakroom... it's just the exact same feeling as when I woke up. Zero appetite. 

I mean, I know I've mentioned it a few times already, but this is really the whole reason I'm sitting here talking to you right now. What made me finally ask for help is that I just barely want to eat anymore, at any point in the day. It's just so bizarre to me. I'll be on my lunch break at the store, staring at food I used to like—food I actually bought because I thought, 'Maybe this time I'll want it'—and I just end up throwing most of it away. And then I go home after my shift, and it's the same story for dinner. I might open the fridge, look inside, close it, and just go sit on the couch. So yeah, it's not like it comes and goes depending on the clock. It's just this heavy, constant blanket over me from the minute I wake up until I go to sleep. Just... nothing. No appetite at all, all day long.
Do you feel numb or disconnected from your emotions when you think about eating?

Yeah, numb is probably a really good word for it, actually. It's like... I don't feel sad when I look at the food, and I don't feel angry or disgusted, I just feel absolutely nothing. Like a dial just got turned all the way down to zero in my head. I'll be looking at it, trying to summon up some kind of feeling, you know? Like, trying to force my brain to go, 'Oh, man, this is gonna taste so good,' or 'I'm so glad I bought this.' But there's just this massive disconnect. It's almost like the food belongs to someone else, or like it's just a plastic prop in a movie, not something I'm actually supposed to chew and swallow. 

I know I keep hammering on this exact same point, Doc, and I know I'm probably driving you crazy repeating myself, but that specific feeling—that disconnected, numb feeling where I just barely want to eat anymore—that is literally what made me ask for help in the first place. It's the whole reason I finally picked up the phone. Because I'll be on my lunch break at the store, right? Just sitting there staring at food I used to really like, trying to feel *something* about it, trying to find that old spark of wanting it, and the connection is just totally severed. I don't feel hungry, I don't feel excited, I just feel completely blank. So I just end up throwing most of it away, just like I was saying before. It's just this really weird, empty feeling whenever food is involved, and I just can't snap out of it.
Do you think your lack of appetite is related to your emotional state?

Yeah, I really do think it's all connected. Because that numb feeling... it's not just happening when I'm sitting in the breakroom looking at my lunch. It's my whole emotional state right now, it's bleeding into literally everything else in my life. 

Like, I used to be a guy who actually did things, you know? I used to get really excited about going to gallery nights downtown, or getting some guys together to play basketball at the park on my days off. I even used to love hitting up those food-trucks for tacos after a game, just hanging out and talking, or spending time helping out the neighborhood kids with their art stuff. I used to get a real kick out of all of that, it used to mean something to me. 

But lately... man, lately it's exactly like how I feel about the food. I'll drag myself out to one of those things because I feel like I'm supposed to, and I just stand there feeling completely flat. There's no spark, no joy in it at all. I'll be standing there on the court, or looking at some kid's painting, and I just feel nothing. My brain is just static. So I usually just end up making some excuse to leave early, like telling them I have a headache or I'm too tired from my shift at the store, and I just go home. 

So yeah, the appetite thing is definitely tied to my emotions. Because if I can't even get excited about basketball or art or hanging out with my friends anymore, it makes total sense that I wouldn't care about eating a sandwich, either. It's all just the exact same flat, empty feeling across the board. It's like my whole personality just got wiped out, and everything I used to care about—whether it's my hobbies or my lunch—is just totally pointless now.
Has there been a significant event or change in your life that you think might be connected to when your appetite started to decrease?

Well, yeah, actually. I mean, it’s not like someone died or I got fired or anything like that, but... yeah, there was this thing that happened at work. It's been going on for about two months now, this whole not wanting to eat and feeling totally blank thing. And it started right around the time I won this... this award at the store. 

See, I usually just stock shelves and deal with customers, right? But a couple of months ago, my manager asked me to help set up the new front window display because she knows I like art and stuff. So I did it, and I guess I did a really good job because the district manager came by for a walkthrough and he made this huge deal out of it. Like, a really big deal. He took pictures, he shook my hand in front of everyone, they gave me this little certificate thing... and suddenly all this attention was on me. 

And you’d think that’d be a good thing, right? Like, 'Hey, good job, man.' But ever since then, ever since that district manager made such a big fuss about the window display... that’s exactly when things started feeling off. That’s when my appetite just packed up and left. It's been about two months of this now, just waking up every single day since that award and feeling like my stomach is tied in a knot and my head is just full of static. I don't know why getting a compliment on a window display would make me stop eating and stop caring about basketball, but the timing is just right there. Two months ago. The award, the district manager, all that attention... and then boom, no appetite. None at all.
Do you think your lack of appetite is more related to your mind or your body?

Honestly, Doc, I really think... I mean, it's got to be my mind, right? Because physically, my stomach doesn't hurt. I don't have a stomach bug, I'm not nauseous, my throat doesn't hurt when I swallow... physically, my body is perfectly fine. It's all up here, in my head. It's my brain doing this. 

And I know I'm probably sounding like a broken record, I know I brought this exact same thing up when we first started talking, but I just can't stress enough how much this is messing with me. Like I was saying earlier, this whole thing—the fact that I barely want to eat anymore—that is exactly what made me ask for help in the first place. Because it just doesn't make any logical sense. My body *should* be hungry. I'm on my feet all day, right? I'm hauling boxes out of the back room, I'm stocking shelves, I'm running back and forth to the registers... physically, I am burning off energy. 

But then my lunch break rolls around. And I'll just be sitting there in the breakroom at the store, and my mind just completely shuts the whole process down. I'll be sitting there, staring at food I used to really like—like a turkey sub from the place next door, or whatever—and my body just gets completely overridden by whatever this static is in my brain. My mind just says, 'No, we don't care about this.' So I just end up throwing most of it away, exactly like I was telling you before. It’s not my stomach rejecting the food, it’s my mind just totally blocking the whole concept of eating. I’ll actually sit there looking at the trash can, thinking about how ridiculous it is that I'm tossing out perfectly good food that I paid for, but I mentally just cannot make myself take a bite. So yeah, it's definitely my mind. It's like my brain just forgot what food is even for.
Do you think your lack of interest in food is related to feelings of stress, anxiety, or depression?

Well, I guess... I mean, yeah, it's depression, or stress, or whatever you want to call it. But it's really tied to this overwhelming feeling that I'm just a fraud. Like, ever since that whole window display thing and the award... I just keep thinking about it, constantly. 

I'll be standing there at the cash register, ringing someone up, and my brain just starts looping on how I don't deserve any of it. I don't deserve that certificate, I don't deserve the praise from the district manager, and they were even hinting at putting me up for a supervisor spot, which is just... it's absurd. I don't deserve that chance, either. I'm just a guy who didn't even finish high school, you know? I dropped out in the 11th grade. I stock shelves. That's what I do. I'm not some creative genius, I'm not management material. 

And it just eats at me. I feel so incredibly guilty, like I somehow tricked the manager, the district manager, everyone in the store. Like I pulled this massive con on them, even though I didn't mean to. I just put some boxes and signs in a window. And now they all think I'm this great employee, and I just feel this crushing guilt all day long. My coworkers will come up to me and say, 'Hey, man, you really deserved that award, the window looks awesome,' and I just want to crawl under the floorboards because I know they're wrong. I know I didn't earn it. I feel like I'm lying to them just by standing there. 

So yeah, when lunchtime comes around and I'm sitting there with that guilt just churning in my stomach, feeling like the biggest fake on the planet... how am I supposed to eat? How can I sit there and enjoy a sandwich when I feel like I've tricked everyone who works with me? It's just this heavy, dark feeling that I'm completely worthless and I don't deserve any of the good things they're trying to give me. So the appetite just goes right out the window. It's all just stress and guilt, 24/7.
Are you afraid that if you start eating, you won't be able to stop?

No, no, it's not like that at all. It's not like I'm scared I'm gonna gorge myself or something. I mean, I know some people deal with that, where they eat and eat and can't stop, but for me, it's the exact opposite. I literally just don't want it. 

If I'm being completely honest, the thought of eating a lot... it just doesn't even compute right now. Like, I was saying about the breakroom, sitting there with a sandwich or whatever. It's not that I'm looking at it thinking, 'Oh man, if I take one bite of this turkey sub, I'm going to end up eating five of them and then go buy a whole pizza.' It's more like I look at that one bite and think, 'I don't deserve this one bite, and also, this one bite feels like it's made of sand.' 

So, no, I'm not afraid of losing control and eating everything in sight. I'm just... I just have zero desire to start. It's like the engine is completely off, you know? There's no fear of the car speeding out of control because the car won't even start in the first place. I just sit there feeling guilty and empty, and the food just sits there until I throw it away. That's the whole cycle. There's no bingeing or anything like that. Just... nothing.

I even used to love hitting up those food-trucks for tacos after a game, just hanging out and talking, or spending time helping out the neighborhood kids with their art stuff. I used to get a real kick out of all of that, it used to mean something to me. 

But lately... man, lately it's exactly like how I feel about the food. I'll drag myself out to one of those things because I feel like I'm supposed to, and I just stand there feeling completely flat. There's no spark, no joy in it at all. I'll be standing there on the court, or looking at some kid's painting, and I just feel nothing. My brain is just static. So I usually just end up making some excuse to leave early, like telling them I have a headache or I'm too tired from my shift at the store, and I just go home. 

So yeah, the appetite thing is definitely tied to my emotions. Because if I can't even get excited about basketball or art or hanging out with my friends anymore, it makes total sense that I wouldn't care about eating a sandwich, either. It's all just the exact same flat, empty feeling across the board. It's like my whole personality just got wiped out, and everything I used to care about—whether it's my hobbies or my lunch—is just totally pointless now.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's lack of appetite is related to a specific emotional state or event
doctor.question: Has there been a significant event or change in your life that you think might be connected to when your appetite started to decrease?

target_item.name: Duration
target_item.manifestation: This has been going on for about two months, since the window display award and all the attention from the district manager.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about the timeline and any significant events connected to the onset of the symptoms, which directly corresponds to the duration profile that mentions the symptoms starting about two months ago after the window display award.

patient.answer:
Well, yeah, actually. I mean, it’s not like someone died or I got fired or anything like that, but... yeah, there was this thing that happened at work. It's been going on for about two months now, this whole not wanting to eat and feeling totally blank thing. And it started right around the time I won this... this award at the store. 

See, I usually just stock shelves and deal with customers, right? But a couple of months ago, my manager asked me to help set up the new front window display because she knows I like art and stuff. So I did it, and I guess I did a really good job because the district manager came by for a walkthrough and he made this huge deal out of it. Like, a really big deal. He took pictures, he shook my hand in front of everyone, they gave me this little certificate thing... and suddenly all this attention was on me. 

And you’d think that’d be a good thing, right? Like, 'Hey, good job, man.' But ever since then, ever since that district manager made such a big fuss about the window display... that’s exactly when things started feeling off. That’s when my appetite just packed up and left. It's been about two months of this now, just waking up every single day since that award and feeling like my stomach is tied in a knot and my head is just full of static. I don't know why getting a compliment on a window display would make me stop eating and stop caring about basketball, but the timing is just right there. Two months ago. The award, the district manager, all that attention... and then boom, no appetite. None at all.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's lack of appetite is a result of a psychological issue or a physical issue
doctor.question: Do you think your lack of appetite is more related to your mind or your body?

target_item.name: Weight_Appetite_Change
target_item.manifestation: What made me ask for help is I barely want to eat anymore, like I will be on my lunch break at the store staring at food I used to like and I just throw most of it away.
target_item.reason: The doctor's question specifically asks about the patient's lack of appetite and whether it stems from a physical (body) or psychological (mind) cause.

patient.answer:
Honestly, Doc, I really think... I mean, it's got to be my mind, right? Because physically, my stomach doesn't hurt. I don't have a stomach bug, I'm not nauseous, my throat doesn't hurt when I swallow... physically, my body is perfectly fine. It's all up here, in my head. It's my brain doing this. 

And I know I'm probably sounding like a broken record, I know I brought this exact same thing up when we first started talking, but I just can't stress enough how much this is messing with me. Like I was saying earlier, this whole thing—the fact that I barely want to eat anymore—that is exactly what made me ask for help in the first place. Because it just doesn't make any logical sense. My body *should* be hungry. I'm on my feet all day, right? I'm hauling boxes out of the back room, I'm stocking shelves, I'm running back and forth to the registers... physically, I am burning off energy. 

But then my lunch break rolls around. And I'll just be sitting there in the breakroom at the store, and my mind just completely shuts the whole process down. I'll be sitting there, staring at food I used to really like—like a turkey sub from the place next door, or whatever—and my body just gets completely overridden by whatever this static is in my brain. My mind just says, 'No, we don't care about this.' So I just end up throwing most of it away, exactly like I was telling you before. It’s not my stomach rejecting the food, it’s my mind just totally blocking the whole concept of eating. I’ll actually sit there looking at the trash can, thinking about how ridiculous it is that I'm tossing out perfectly good food that I paid for, but I mentally just cannot make myself take a bite. So yeah, it's definitely my mind. It's like my brain just forgot what food is even for.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's lack of appetite is related to a specific psychological condition
doctor.question: Do you think your lack of interest in food is related to feelings of stress, anxiety, or depression?

target_item.name: Worthlessness_Guilt
target_item.manifestation: I keep thinking I do not deserve the award or the chance at supervisor, and I feel guilty like I tricked everyone even though people tell me I did not.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking if the appetite loss is related to feelings of stress, anxiety, or depression. The patient can explain their depressive feelings by describing their inappropriate guilt and feelings of worthlessness regarding the award.

patient.answer:
Well, I guess... I mean, yeah, it's depression, or stress, or whatever you want to call it. But it's really tied to this overwhelming feeling that I'm just a fraud. Like, ever since that whole window display thing and the award... I just keep thinking about it, constantly. 

I'll be standing there at the cash register, ringing someone up, and my brain just starts looping on how I don't deserve any of it. I don't deserve that certificate, I don't deserve the praise from the district manager, and they were even hinting at putting me up for a supervisor spot, which is just... it's absurd. I don't deserve that chance, either. I'm just a guy who didn't even finish high school, you know? I dropped out in the 11th grade. I stock shelves. That's what I do. I'm not some creative genius, I'm not management material. 

And it just eats at me. I feel so incredibly guilty, like I somehow tricked the manager, the district manager, everyone in the store. Like I pulled this massive con on them, even though I didn't mean to. I just put some boxes and signs in a window. And now they all think I'm this great employee, and I just feel this crushing guilt all day long. My coworkers will come up to me and say, 'Hey, man, you really deserved that award, the window looks awesome,' and I just want to crawl under the floorboards because I know they're wrong. I know I didn't earn it. I feel like I'm lying to them just by standing there. 

So yeah, when lunchtime comes around and I'm sitting there with that guilt just churning in my stomach, feeling like the biggest fake on the planet... how am I supposed to eat? How can I sit there and enjoy a sandwich when I feel like I've tricked everyone who works with me? It's just this heavy, dark feeling that I'm completely worthless and I don't deserve any of the good things they're trying to give me. So the appetite just goes right out the window. It's all just stress and guilt, 24/7.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's lack of appetite is related to a fear of being unable to control their eating
doctor.question: Are you afraid that if you start eating, you won't be able to stop?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about a fear of losing control over eating (binge eating), which is a symptom of eating disorders and is not covered by the patient's profile.

patient.answer:
No, no, it's not like that at all. It's not like I'm scared I'm gonna gorge myself or something. I mean, I know some people deal with that, where they eat and eat and can't stop, but for me, it's the exact opposite. I literally just don't want it. 

If I'm being completely honest, the thought of eating a lot... it just doesn't even compute right now. Like, I was saying about the breakroom, sitting there with a sandwich or whatever. It's not that I'm looking at it thinking, 'Oh man, if I take one bite of this turkey sub, I'm going to end up eating five of them and then go buy a whole pizza.' It's more like I look at that one bite and think, 'I don't deserve this one bite, and also, this one bite feels like it's made of sand.' 

So, no, I'm not afraid of losing control and eating everything in sight. I'm just... I just have zero desire to start. It's like the engine is completely off, you know? There's no fear of the car speeding out of control because the car won't even start in the first place. I just sit there feeling guilty and empty, and the food just sits there until I throw it away. That's the whole cycle. There's no bingeing or anything like that. Just... nothing.
